title: Split finite-free map residue localization with explicit inverses
statement: For a commutative ring R, finite free map u : R^m → R^n and prime p, injectivity on the residue-field base change implies there is f not in p for which the localized map has a left inverse and its cokernel is finite and free. Bijectivity on the residue-field base change implies there is f not in p for which the localized map has both a left and a right inverse.

source.place: Tag 00O0, Lemma cokernel-flat, parts (1) and (3), finite-free matrix calculation

proof.text: Over the residue field, the matrix of u has rank m by injectivity. Row rank equals column rank (Mathlib Matrix.rank_eq_finrank_span_row), so the rows span the m-dimensional coordinate space. Choose a basis among those rows using Basis.ofSpan and reindex it by Fin m. The corresponding row embedding selects a square minor with nonzero determinant. Determinants commute with scalar extension, and Ideal.algebraMap_residueField_eq_zero shows that its determinant f in R lies outside p.

Localize at f. In the induced bases the selected minor B has unit determinant. Define the retraction by projecting onto the selected rows, multiplying by B inverse, and converting back from source coordinates. Both matrix inverse identities give v u = id and equality between selected coordinates of u(v(y)) and y. Let C be the finite complement of the selected rows. Define q(y) to be the C coordinates of y - u(v(y)). Its kernel is the image of u: on selected rows use B B inverse = id, and on the complement use q(y)=0. It is surjective by extending any C-coordinate vector by zero on the selected rows. The first isomorphism theorem identifies the cokernel with C -> R_f, hence it is finite and free.

For bijective residue-field base change, equality of dimensions gives m=n. Apply the preceding construction to its injective part. The localized source and target are now the same finite free module, and LinearMap.comp_eq_id_comm over the commutative localization ring turns the left inverse identity into the right inverse identity. This uses the inverse of the selected square minor and requires no further localization.

proof_origin.place: Tag 00O0, Lemma cokernel-flat, parts (1) and (3); finite-free matrix calculation, implemented using a row basis and an explicit cokernel projection

lean.statement: theorem finiteFreeMap_residue_localization_strong {R : Type*} [CommRing R] (m n : ℕ) (u : (Fin m → R) →ₗ[R] (Fin n → R)) (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime] : (Function.Injective (u.baseChange p.ResidueField) → ∃ f : R, f ∉ p ∧ (∃ v : TensorProduct R (Localization.Away f) (Fin n → R) →ₗ[Localization.Away f] TensorProduct R (Localization.Away f) (Fin m → R), v.comp (u.baseChange (Localization.Away f)) = LinearMap.id ∧ Module.Finite (Localization.Away f) (TensorProduct R (Localization.Away f) (Fin n → R) ⧸ LinearMap.range (u.baseChange (Localization.Away f))) ∧ Module.Free (Localization.Away f) (TensorProduct R (Localization.Away f) (Fin n → R) ⧸ LinearMap.range (u.baseChange (Localization.Away f))))) ∧ (Function.Bijective (u.baseChange p.ResidueField) → ∃ f : R, f ∉ p ∧ ∃ v : TensorProduct R (Localization.Away f) (Fin n → R) →ₗ[Localization.Away f] TensorProduct R (Localization.Away f) (Fin m → R), v.comp (u.baseChange (Localization.Away f)) = LinearMap.id ∧ (u.baseChange (Localization.Away f)).comp v = LinearMap.id)
